title: 2007 AMC 12B Problem 3
statement: The point \(O\) is the center of the circle circumscribed about \(\triangle ABC,\) with \(\angle BOC=120^\circ\) and \(\angle AOB=140^\circ,\) as shown. What is the degree measure of \(\angle ABC?\)

solutions.text:
The angles around \(O\) sum to \(360^\circ,\) so \[ \begin{aligned} \angle AOC&=360^\circ-140^\circ-120^\circ \\ &=100^\circ. \end{aligned} \]

By the inscribed angle theorem, \(\angle ABC\) subtends the same arc \(AC\) as the central angle \(\angle AOC,\) so \[ \angle ABC=\tfrac12\angle AOC=50^\circ. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The three central angles at \(O\) add up to \(360^\circ\)
The inscribed angle \(\angle ABC\) is half of the central angle \(\angle AOC\)
